name: EasyDMARC
summary: DMARC, SPF and DKIM monitoring to stop others sending email as your domain.
best_for: anyone who sends email from their own domain and has not yet got DMARC to enforcement: the reporting is the part that makes that safe rather than guesswork
skip_if: you have one domain, send little email, and are willing to read raw XML reports yourself, because EasyDMARC's free record checkers and XML report analyzer plus patience cover the same ground
honest_knock: You are buying domains and history, not features, and no longer seats, since every tier now lists unlimited users. Plus covers two domains. Subdomains do not count toward that, the page says they are detected automatically, but a company with a main domain, a second brand and a legacy domain it forgot about is already over. The history window is the part that bites later: three months on Plus means that when you are investigating a spoofing campaign that started in the spring, the reports are gone. And watch the volume ceiling. Read on 4 October 2026, the page's own tooltip says that once you pass your monthly quota, additional reports are not processed until the next billing cycle. There is no overage charge, just a gap in the data, and it opens precisely when a spoofing run inflates your report volume. Size the plan on your busiest month, not your average.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-04 and again 2026-10-21 on easydmarc.com/pricing, which now redirects to /pricing/businesses; the four amounts are unchanged since 26 August 2026, the plan structure around them changed by 4 October and was the same on 21 October) Plus is 44.99 a month, or 35.99 billed annually, for 2 domains, three months of report history and a monthly volume selector of 100,000, 500,000 or 1,000,000 messages. Premium is 89.99, or 71.99 annually, for 4 domains, a year of history and up to 5,000,000 messages, adding AI agents that read the reports, proactive DMARC alerts, EasySPF, email support and a dedicated CS manager on the yearly plan only. Both open with a free trial and no credit card. Users are now unlimited on every tier, where on 17 September Plus allowed one invited user. The former Enterprise tier is split into two quoted plans: Deliverability (up to unlimited domains, custom volume, up to three years of history, DNS Manager and Sender Insights, delivery analytics, reputation monitoring and inbox placement tests, a dedicated DMARC engineer as a paid add-on) and Enterprise: Email Trust (adding Threat Intelligence, an included DMARC engineer, SSO, API access and audit logs). The page no longer lists a Free plan. Subdomains are detected automatically and do not count toward the domain limit. Past the monthly quota, the page's own tooltip says additional reports are not processed until the next billing cycle. Annual billing is marked Save 20% plus bonus features, and MSPs get a separate tab. On the currency: read from the Netherlands the page prints these as euro amounts and read over a US connection as the identical dollar figures, so €44.99 there is $44.99 here: the symbol changes and the number does not.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested EasyDMARC on the platform trial: adding our own domain, the first result, the verification route, the price of the plans and the checkout up to the card form. No DNS was changed and nothing was paid. Add Domain first offers Discovered Domains, which asks to connect providers such as Mailgun, Amazon SES, SendGrid, HubSpot, Klaviyo and HighLevel; we chose Add Manually. Our domain was added as type Sending (the other choice is Parked) at about 17:28. The step Verify Domain Manually followed: EasyDMARC recognised Hostinger as the DNS provider and says to delete the current DMARC record of type TXT at host _dmarc and then to add a new CNAME record with a value under easydmarc.pro. So verifying means removing your own DMARC record and letting EasyDMARC host DMARC through a CNAME (managed DMARC); stopping later means putting your own record back, which is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later: a DNS change needs a separate approval from the account owner, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified. The domain list showed Policy None, Total Volume 0 and a warning triangle. A domain overview was available within a minute and was viewed at 17:29: Infrastructure Health Score, Total Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100. Authentication showed DMARC Policy None, DMARC Record Valid, SPF Valid (3/10 lookups) and DKIM No Record with Selectors N/A; DMARC Compliance Rate was 0%. Blocklist was Inactive with Monitoring off and Google Postmaster had No data. Our own dig check at 17:29 showed that the _dmarc TXT record is v=DMARC1; p=none, so the policy None is right, and that the SPF record includes the Hostinger mail servers, which is right. The DKIM selector hostingermail-a is a CNAME to the DKIM host of the mail provider with a valid RSA key. So our domain does have DKIM, and EasyDMARC reported No Record, presumably because it does not know the selector until reports arrive, which only happens after the CNAME verification. Pending Actions showed 1 Critical, Verify your domain to unlock full visibility; without verification no DMARC reports arrive. No kit records were entered.
findings: Our own domain was added on the platform trial at about 17:28 and a domain overview was available within a minute: Infrastructure Health Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100.

EasyDMARC read our DMARC policy (none) and SPF (valid, 3 of 10 lookups) correctly, as our own dig check confirmed. It showed DKIM as No Record, although our domain publishes a valid DKIM key for the selector hostingermail-a. The tool does not know the selector until reports arrive.

Verifying the domain means deleting your own DMARC TXT record at _dmarc and adding a CNAME to an easydmarc.pro host, so EasyDMARC hosts DMARC for you. Putting the old record back after leaving is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified.
Without verification no DMARC reports arrive. Pending Actions showed 1 Critical, Verify your domain to unlock full visibility.

There is no free plan in the app: the trial is 14 days without a card, then you pick a paid plan. Yearly billing showed DMARC Plus at 35.99 euros a month (44.99 crossed out) for 2 domains and 3 months of history, and Premium at 71.99 euros. Monthly billing showed Plus at 44.99 euros.
Checkout asks for card number, expiry date and CVV before it shows a purchase summary. We stopped there and entered nothing.
not_tested: We did not watch the original sign-up; the account was already open when our session began.
We did not finish the CNAME verification, so no real DMARC reports arrived. Email provider connections, AI Agents, DNS Manager, Sender Insights, Threat Intelligence, the API and MCP stayed closed.
We did not contact support, invite anyone, enter card details, or export and re-import data.
Account deletion, and putting an old DMARC record back after leaving, were not tried.
We did not examine roles, API entitlement or a downgrade.
Session date 15 November 2026, Europe/Amsterdam time. Our clock readings are approximate and not a benchmark.
